 The ground breaking science behind an iconic Cher hit
 The Independent Thursday 12 November 2026 06:36 EST 
 Bookmark popover
 Removed from bookmarks
 Close popover Cher ( Getty ) Author Lior Phillips has released a new book examining Cher 's 1998 album Believe and the groundbreaking science behind its hit lead single.
 AutoTune was originally invented in 1997 by former geophysical engineer Dr Andy Hildebrand as a subtle studio tool to correct pitch.
 Cher and producer Mark Taylor adapted the software for Believe by setting the pitch adjustment speed to zero, creating a striking vocal effect.
 The exaggerated pitch correction became known as the Cher effect, transforming AutoTune from a hidden correction technique into a mainstream artistic choice.
 The track's monumental success cemented Cher's status as an enduring pop icon and fully re-established her artistic independence.
